definition_zh: 透露；揭露；使显露
definition_en: to make known information that was hidden or secret
core_image: 一只手把压在抽屉底的文件抽出来，放到灯下
scene: 记者把录音笔往前推了推，对面的人终于松了口。The company refused to disclose the terms of the deal.
sceneCN: 这里 disclose 指「透露」（第 1 个义项：把隐藏的信息说出来）；句意是公司拒绝透露交易条款。

senses.title: To make information known
senses.definition: to give out facts that were not known to others
senses.definitionCN: 把别人不知道的事实说出来
senses.example: The company refused to disclose the terms of the deal.
senses.exampleCN: 公司拒绝透露交易条款。
senses.why: A fact kept behind a door changes the moment the door opens.
senses.whyCN: 关在门后的事实，在门开的那一刻就变了。

senses.title: To expose a hidden truth
senses.definition: to reveal something wrong or secret that was covered up
senses.definitionCN: 把被掩盖的错误或秘密揭出来
senses.example: The report disclosed serious failures in the system.
senses.exampleCN: 报告揭露了系统中的严重失职。
senses.why: What was buried is suddenly standing in daylight.
senses.whyCN: 原本被埋着的东西，忽然站到了日光下。

senses.title: To uncover to view
senses.definition: to remove a cover so that something can be seen
senses.definitionCN: 揭开遮挡，让某物能被看见
senses.example: The curtain rose and disclosed a bare stage.
senses.exampleCN: 幕布升起，露出空荡的舞台。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply cloth pulled away from a thing.
senses.whyCN: 最老的意思，不过是把布从东西上拉开。

intro.en: Disclose is dis-, the reverse of an action, plus close, from Latin claudere, to shut.
intro.cn: disclose 是表示反动作的 dis- 加 close，而 close 来自拉丁语 claudere（关闭）。

items.en: Claudere meant to shut or to close a door.
items.cn: claudere 指关闭或把门合上。

items.en: Clos meant shut or enclosed, and gave English close.
items.cn: clos 指关闭的、围住的，给出英语 close。

items.en: Disclose first meant to open something that was shut.
items.cn: disclose 最初指把关着的东西打开。

items.en: The word turned toward secrets and hidden facts.
items.cn: 这个词转向秘密与隐藏的事实。

items.en: It now covers company reports and official records.
items.cn: 如今它常用于公司报告与官方记录。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the close stem, while the meaning group names other ways of bringing facts to light.
note.cn: 形近组共用 close 这一段词干，近义组则列出其他让事实见光的说法。

definition_zh: v. 停止；中断；不再继续；停产；停供
definition_en: to stop doing, making or providing something that had been continuing
core_image: 一条一直往前走的传送带被一只手按下停止键，后面的货不再出来
scene: 厂家去年停产了这个型号。The maker discontinued the model last year.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：厂家不再生产某个型号，产品线到此为止。

senses.title: Stop an activity
senses.definition: to stop doing something that you had been doing regularly
senses.definitionCN: （动词）停止原本一直在做的某件事
senses.example: She discontinued the treatment after six weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 六周之后她停止了治疗。

senses.whyCN: 处方笺上最后一行被划掉。

senses.title: Stop making or supplying
senses.definition: to stop producing or providing a product or service
senses.definitionCN: （动词）不再生产或提供某种产品或服务
senses.example: The factory discontinued the model last year.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂去年停产了这个型号。
senses.why: A shop shelf where one product never comes back.
senses.whyCN: 商店货架上某样产品再也不补货。

senses.title: Break the continuity
senses.definition: to interrupt a continuous line, series or process

senses.example: The fence was discontinued where the path crossed.
senses.exampleCN: 围栏在小路穿过的地方中断了。
senses.why: A fence with a gap where a path crosses it.
senses.whyCN: 围栏在小路穿过处留出一个缺口。

intro.en: Discontinue is dis- plus continue; continue goes back through Old French continuer to Latin continuare, to make unbroken, from continuus and the root tenere, to hold.
intro.cn: discontinue 由 dis-（离开、否定）加 continue（继续）构成；continue 经古法语 continuer 上溯拉丁语 continuare「使连接不断」，来自 continuus，最深的词根是 tenere「握住、保持」。

items.en: Latin tenere means to hold or keep.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tenere 意为握住、保持。

items.en: From con- plus tenere came continuus, unbroken.
items.cn: 由 con- 加 tenere 得到 continuus，意为不间断的。

items.en: Continuare meant to join things without a break.
items.cn: continuare 意为把东西连接起来不留断口。

items.en: Old French continuer carried the sense of keeping on.
items.cn: 古法语 continuer 承接了继续下去的意思。

items.en: Middle English contynuen entered the language as continue.
items.cn: 中古英语 contynuen 进入英语成为 continue。

items.en: The prefix dis- was added to give discontinue, to stop keeping on.
items.cn: 加上前缀 dis- 得到 discontinue，意为不再继续。

note.en: Discontinue is continue with a negative prefix; its neighbours either keep the same root or mean stopping.
note.cn: discontinue 是 continue 加否定前缀；它的邻居要么同词根，要么表示停止。

intro.en: Discord is dis-, apart, plus cor, heart; the same heart root builds accord, concord and cordial, so discord literally means hearts apart.

items.en: Latin cor means heart, the seat of feeling.

items.en: The prefix dis- means apart or away.

items.en: Discordare meant to be at variance, hearts apart.

items.en: The musical sense of harsh sounding notes appears later.

note.en: Discord sits between two heart words that mean the opposite, and three words for conflict.

senses.definition: to decide that a story or a risk need not be taken seriously
senses.definitionCN: 认为某个说法或风险不必当真
senses.example: We should not discount the risk of delay.
senses.exampleCN: 我们不该轻视延误的风险。
senses.why: The mind also crosses out what it does not wish to count.
senses.whyCN: 脑子也会划掉它不愿计入的东西。

intro.en: Discount came from dis- plus count, literally to count off a part, and passed through Italian and French.
intro.cn: discount 是 dis- 加 count，字面是「扣掉一部分再算」，经意大利语与法语传来。

items.en: Computare meant to reckon together, the base of count.
items.cn: computare 指合起来计算，是 count 的词源。

items.en: Disconto named a sum counted off from a debt.
items.cn: disconto 指从欠款里扣掉的数目。

items.en: Descompte carried the money sense into French trade.
items.cn: descompte 把这个钱的用法带进法国商业。

items.en: Discount named money taken off a price.
items.cn: discount 指从价钱里减去的钱。

items.en: The verb widened to mean treating an idea as not worth counting.
items.cn: 动词义后来扩展到「不把某个说法算进去」。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the count stem, while the meaning group names other price cuts.
note.cn: 形近组共用 count 这一段词干，近义组则列出其他减价说法。

entries.definition: to say numbers in order or to include something
entries.definitionCN: 按顺序数数，或把某物算进去

entries.definition: a record of money kept at a bank
entries.definitionCN: 银行里的存款记录

entries.definition: able to be counted one by one
entries.definitionCN: 可以逐个计数的

entries.definition: a lowering of price or amount
entries.definitionCN: 价格或数量的降低

entries.definition: money returned after a payment
entries.definitionCN: 付款后退回的一部分钱

entries.definition: an amount taken away from a total
entries.definitionCN: 从总数中扣除的数额

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a crossed-out price to a risk that is quietly left out of the count.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从被划掉的价格，走到被悄悄排除在计算之外的风险。

normal.en: Dis- plus count: count a little less.
normal.cn: dis- 加 count：少算一点。

normal.en: A discount is a number crossed out with a smile.
normal.cn: 折扣就是一个被笑着划掉的数字。

normal.en: Student discount asks who you are before what you buy.
normal.cn: 学生优惠先问你是谁，再问你买什么。

normal.en: To discount a warning is to leave it out of the sum.
normal.cn: 轻视一个警告，就是把它从总数里漏掉。

normal.en: The same word lowers a price and lowers a risk.
normal.cn: 同一个词，既压低价钱，也压低风险的分量。

abstract.en: Picture a red line through an old price.
abstract.cn: 想象旧价钱上划过一道红线。

abstract.en: Picture a smaller number written in the corner.
abstract.cn: 想象角落里写着一个更小的数。

abstract.en: Picture a warning note moved to the bottom of a pile.
abstract.cn: 想象一张警告纸条被挪到一摞纸的最下面。

examples.en: The shop gave students a ten per cent discount.
examples.cn: 这家店给学生打九折。

examples.en: The old stock was discounted by half.
examples.cn: 旧货打了对折。

examples.en: We should not discount the risk of delay.
examples.cn: 我们不该轻视延误的风险。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 discount 记成「的士扛」：的士费太贵，扛着东西走，店家只好给个折扣。

root: 由 dis-（去掉）加 count（计算）构成，字面意思是「扣掉一部分再算」。这个词经意大利语 disconto 与法语 descompte 进入英语，先指从欠款或价钱里减去的数目，后来也作动词表示打折，并引申为把某种说法或风险排除在考虑之外。

sensesIntro.en: From money taken off a price, to the act of lowering it, to a risk left out of the count.
sensesIntro.cn: 从价钱里减掉的钱，到把价钱压低这个动作，再到被排除在计算之外的风险。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old price crossed out, a smaller number beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：旧价钱被划掉，旁边写着一个更小的数。

chain: PART OF IT IS STRUCK OUT

branches.en: The first sense is the sum taken off the price.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是从价钱里减掉的那笔钱。

branches.en: The second sense is the act of lowering the price.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是把价钱压低的动作。

branches.en: The third sense is a claim left out of the count.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是被排除在计算之外的说法。

branches.en: The amount and the act both make the number smaller.
branches.cn: 金额与动作，都让那个数字变小。

branches.en: A price and a risk can both be counted for less.
branches.cn: 价钱和风险，都可以被算得更轻。

intro.en: Discount belongs to the count family, words about reckoning and accounts.
intro.cn: discount 属于 count 一族，围绕计算与账目。

latinIntro.en: Latin computare, to reckon together, gives count, account and discount.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 computare（合起来计算）给出 count、account 与 discount。

items.meaning: a sum counted off a price
items.example: The discount brought the price down.

items.meaning: to reckon numbers or include something
items.example: Count the chairs before you order.

items.meaning: a record of money or an explanation
items.example: He opened an account at the bank.

items.meaning: a person who keeps financial records
not able to be counted one by one
able to be sold at a lower price

definition_zh: 使气馁；劝阻
definition_en: to make someone feel less confident, or to try to stop someone from doing something
core_image: 一只手刚抬起来要往前，另一只手从旁边轻轻把它按下去
scene: 报名表还摊在桌上，笔尖停在半空。One failed attempt should not discourage you.
sceneCN: 这里 discourage 指「使气馁」（第 1 个义项：让人失去信心）；句意是一次失败不该让你泄气。

senses.title: To drain the will to try
senses.definition: to make someone feel less confident or less hopeful
senses.definitionCN: 让人失去信心或希望
senses.example: One bad grade should not discourage you.
senses.exampleCN: 一次糟糕的成绩不该让你气馁。
senses.why: Courage is a supply, and a few cold words can empty it.
senses.whyCN: 勇气像一份存量，几句冷话就能把它掏空。

senses.title: To talk someone out of an act
senses.definition: to try to stop someone from doing something by pointing at doubt or difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 用怀疑或困难让对方打消做某事的念头
senses.example: The teacher discouraged us from copying answers.
senses.exampleCN: 老师劝我们不要抄答案。
senses.why: A hand raised to stop is gentler than a door slammed shut.
senses.whyCN: 抬手拦住，比摔门关上要温和。

intro.en: Discourage joins dis-, meaning away, to the Latin cor, the heart, so the word pictures courage being taken out of the chest.
intro.cn: discourage 由表示「拿走」的 dis- 与拉丁语的心 cor 组成，画面是把勇气从胸口取走。

items.en: Cor, cordis meant the heart, and Romans placed courage there.
items.cn: cor 指心，罗马人把勇气安放在心里。

items.en: Descoragier meant to strip away heart or spirit.
items.cn: 古法语 descoragier 指把心气剥掉。

items.en: English borrowed it to mean deprive of courage.
items.cn: 英语借入后表示使失去勇气。

items.en: The sense widened to holding someone back from an act.
items.cn: 词义扩大，也指拦住别人不让做某事。

items.en: Today it covers both a lost heart and a friendly warning.
items.cn: 今天它既指心里泄气，也指好言拦阻。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the courage stem, while the meaning group gathers words for warning someone off.
note.cn: 形近组共享 courage 这一段，近义组则是几个表示劝退或泄气的词。

entries.definition: the strength to face fear
entries.definitionCN: 面对恐惧的力量

entries.definition: to give someone hope or support
entries.definitionCN: 给人希望或支持

entries.definition: the feeling of lost hope
entries.definitionCN: 希望落空的感觉

entries.definition: to make someone decide not to act
entries.definitionCN: 让人决定不做

entries.definition: to take away hope or spirit
entries.definitionCN: 拿走希望或心气

entries.definition: to persuade someone not to do something
entries.definitionCN: 说服某人不做某事

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the picture of a hand pressing another hand down.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子守住一幅画面：一只手把另一只手按下去。

normal.en: Dis- plus courage means courage taken out.
normal.cn: dis 加 courage，就是把勇气拿走。

normal.en: A coach who lists only failures discourages the whole team.
normal.cn: 教练只数落失败，整支队伍都会泄气。

normal.en: One cold comment can discourage a new learner.
normal.cn: 一句冷话就能让新学的人泄气。

normal.en: Friends discourage you from quitting by naming the risk.
normal.cn: 朋友点出风险，劝你别辞职。

normal.en: Discouraged parents stop asking the school for changes.
normal.cn: 心灰意冷的家长不再向学校提要求。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressing another hand gently down.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手轻轻把另一只手按下去。

abstract.en: Picture a balloon losing air until it lies flat.
abstract.cn: 想象一只气球漏气，最后瘪在地上。

abstract.en: Picture a voice at the door saying not yet.
abstract.cn: 想象门口有个声音说，再等等。

examples.en: Do not let one bad review discourage you.
examples.cn: 别让一条差评让你泄气。

examples.en: The rain discouraged most of the visitors.
examples.cn: 这场雨让大多数游客打消了念头。

examples.en: She was discouraged by the long waiting list.
examples.cn: 长长的等候名单让她泄了气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 discourage 记成「抽走勇气」：dis 是拿走，courage 是勇气，勇气被拿走，人就泄气，也会劝人别做。

root: 来自古法语 descoragier，词根是拉丁语 cor（心），加前缀 dis- 表示拿走，本义是把心气抽走。英语里先指使人失去勇气，后也指用言语劝人放弃某件事。

sensesIntro.en: From a heart that loses its nerve, to a friend who talks you out of the plan.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一颗失去底气的心，到一位劝你放弃计划的朋友。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressed gently down on another hand as it starts to rise.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手刚刚抬起，另一只手轻轻把它按下去。

branches.en: The first sense is the inward loss of nerve.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是心里那点底气被抽走。

branches.en: The second sense turns that loss into advice for someone else.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把这种泄气变成对别人的劝告。

branches.en: Both senses remove the will before the act begins.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在行动开始前先拿走意愿。

branches.en: Both can be caused by a single sentence from a stranger.
branches.cn: 两个义项都可能被陌生人的一句话造成。

branches.en: Only the second sense needs another person in front of you.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项需要眼前另有一个人才成立。

intro.en: Discourage gathers the courage family, with Latin cor, the heart, at its centre.
intro.cn: discourage 聚起 courage 一族，中心是拉丁语里表示心的 cor。

latinIntro.en: Latin cor, heart, gives cord- and courage; dis- and en- push the same stem in opposite directions.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cor（心）给出 cord 与 courage，前缀 dis- 与 en- 把同一词干推向相反方向。

items.meaning: the heart as the seat of bravery
items.example: It takes courage to speak first.
Her note encouraged the whole class.
He sounded discouraged on the phone.
items.exampleCN: 他在电话里听起来很泄气。

items.meaning: in a way that kills hope
items.example: She spoke discouragingly of the plan.
items.exampleCN: 她谈起这个计划时很泄气。

definition_zh: adj. 无礼的；粗鲁的；失礼的
definition_en: lacking politeness or good manners; rude
core_image: 别人话还没说完，一只手就横着切过去；门口的迎宾垫被踢到一边
scene: 打断别人说话是很失礼的。It is discourteous to interrupt.
sceneCN: 第 3 个义项：话没说完就被打断，礼数上失了分寸。

senses.title: Lacking good manners
senses.definition: not showing the politeness expected in a situation
senses.definitionCN: （形容词）没有表现出场合所要求的礼貌
senses.example: It was discourteous to leave without saying goodbye.
senses.exampleCN: 不辞而别是很失礼的。
senses.why: A guest leaving without a word of goodbye.
senses.whyCN: 一位客人不辞而别。

senses.title: Rude in manner
senses.definition: showing a rough or offhand way of treating people
senses.definitionCN: （形容词）以生硬或随便的方式对待别人
senses.example: His discourteous manner upset the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 他粗鲁的态度让整个团队都不舒服。
senses.why: A reply written with no greeting at all.
senses.whyCN: 一封连称呼都没有的回信。

senses.title: Breaking a social rule
senses.definition: going against an accepted rule of polite behaviour
senses.definitionCN: （形容词）违背公认的礼貌规矩
senses.example: It is discourteous to interrupt a speaker.
senses.exampleCN: 打断发言者是失礼的。
senses.why: A hand cutting across someone still speaking.
senses.whyCN: 一只手横着切过还在说话的人。

intro.en: Discourteous is dis- plus courteous; courteous comes from court, which goes back through Old French curt to Latin cortem, an enclosed yard or court, so it once meant having the manners of the court.
intro.cn: discourteous 是 dis-（否定）加 courteous（有礼貌的）；courteous 来自 court（宫廷），court 经古法语 curt 上溯拉丁语 cortem「围院、宫廷」，本义是「有宫廷中人的举止」。

items.en: Latin cors, cortis meant a court or enclosed yard.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cors、cortis 意为宫廷或围起来的院子。

items.en: Old French curt referred to the royal court.
items.cn: 古法语 curt 指国王的宫廷。

items.en: Curteis meant having the manners of the court.
items.cn: curteis 意为有宫廷中人的举止。

items.en: Middle English curteis became courteous, polite.
items.cn: 中古英语 curteis 变成 courteous，意为有礼貌的。

items.en: The negative prefix dis- produced discourteous.
items.cn: 加上否定前缀 dis- 得到 discourteous。

items.en: Today it is a formal word for rude behaviour.
items.cn: 今天它是形容粗鲁行为的正式用词。

note.en: Discourteous is courteous with a negative prefix; the plain word for it is rude.
note.cn: discourteous 是 courteous 加否定前缀；它的日常说法是 rude。

entries.definition: polite and respectful in manner
entries.definitionCN: 举止有礼而尊重人的

entries.definition: polite behaviour or a kind favour
entries.definitionCN: 礼貌的举止或好意的帮忙

entries.definition: rude behaviour; an act of bad manners
entries.definitionCN: 粗鲁的行为；失礼的举动

entries.definition: not polite; the everyday word for it
entries.definitionCN: 不礼貌的；日常用词

entries.definition: failing to show good manners
entries.definitionCN: 没有表现出良好举止的

entries.definition: using few words in a way that seems rude
entries.definitionCN: 说话简短生硬，显得无礼的

normalIntro.en: Five pictures of manners missing from the room.
normalIntro.cn: 五个礼数缺席的画面。

normal.en: A hand cutting across someone still speaking.
normal.cn: 一只手横着切过还在说话的人。

normal.en: A guest leaving without a word of goodbye.
normal.cn: 一位客人不辞而别。

normal.en: A welcome mat kicked off to one side.
normal.cn: 一张迎宾垫被踢到一边。

normal.en: A reply written with no greeting at all.
normal.cn: 一封连称呼都没有的回信。

normal.en: A finger pointing at a guest across the table.
normal.cn: 一根手指隔着餐桌指向客人。

abstract.en: A guest leaving without a word of goodbye.
abstract.cn: 一位客人不辞而别。

abstract.en: A reply written with no greeting at all.
abstract.cn: 一封连称呼都没有的回信。

abstract.en: A hand cutting across someone still speaking.
abstract.cn: 一只手横着切过还在说话的人。

examples.en: She thought the reply discourteous.
examples.cn: 她觉得那个答复很无礼。

examples.en: Such discourteous behaviour cannot be ignored.
examples.cn: 这样失礼的行为不能置之不理。

examples.en: It is discourteous to stare at guests.
examples.cn: 盯着客人看是失礼的。

dict_mnemonic.text: discourteous ＝ dis-（否定）＋ courteous（有礼貌的）；courteous 来自 court（宫廷），court 又来自拉丁语 cortem「围院、宫廷」＝宫廷里该有的举止没有了，「无礼的」。

root: 拉丁语 cors／cortem（宫廷）→ 古法语 curt → curteis（有宫廷举止的）→ 英语 courteous → 加 dis- 成 discourteous

sensesIntro.en: Manners missing: a silent goodbye, a rough manner and a hand cutting across a speaker.
sensesIntro.cn: 缺席的礼数：无声的告别、生硬的态度与横着切过发言者的手。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a welcome mat kicked aside while a hand cuts across someone still speaking
core.cn: 核心意象：迎宾垫被踢到一边，一只手横着切过还在说话的人

branches.en: A guest leaving without a goodbye.
branches.cn: 不辞而别的客人。

branches.en: A rough manner that upsets a team.
branches.cn: 让团队不舒服的生硬态度。

branches.en: A hand cutting across a speaker.
branches.cn: 横着切过发言者的手。

branches.en: Both leave the other person feeling small.
branches.cn: 两者都让对方觉得被看轻。

branches.en: Both cross a line others expect you to keep.
branches.cn: 两者都越过别人期待你守住的界线。

intro.en: Discourteous is dis- plus courteous; the court root also builds courtesy and courtier, while polite comes from a different root meaning to polish.
intro.cn: discourteous 由 dis- 加 courteous 构成；宫廷这个词根也造出 courtesy 与 courtier，而 polite 来自另一个意为磨光的词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin cors means an enclosed court, Old French curteis meant of the court, and Latin polire means to polish.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cors 意为围起来的宫廷，古法语 curteis 意为宫廷的，拉丁语 polire 意为磨光。

definition_zh: 发现；发觉
definition_en: to find something or learn a fact for the first time
core_image: 草丛被拨开，地上露出一只从没被记录的脚印
scene: 雨后的泥地很软，他蹲下去看那串新鲜的痕迹。She discovered a hidden path behind the house.
sceneCN: 这里 discover 指「发现」（第 1 个义项：找到原本存在却不为人知的东西）；句意是她发现屋后有一条隐蔽的小路。

collocations.phrase: discover that the door was open

senses.title: To come upon what was hidden
senses.definition: to find something that existed before but was not known
senses.definitionCN: 找到原本存在却不为人知的东西
senses.example: Scientists discovered a new kind of frog.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家发现了一种新的青蛙。
senses.why: A page turns, and a room that was always there appears.
senses.whyCN: 翻过一页，一间一直都在的屋子忽然出现。

senses.title: To learn a fact
senses.definition: to learn or realize something you did not know before
senses.definitionCN: 得知或意识到自己原先不知道的事
senses.example: I discovered that the shop closes at six.
senses.exampleCN: 我发觉那家店六点关门。
senses.why: The world does not change; only your picture of it does.
senses.whyCN: 世界没变，变的是你心里那张图。

intro.en: Discover is Latin dis-, undoing, plus cooperire, to cover: to take the cover off something.
intro.cn: discover 是拉丁语 dis-（去掉）加 cooperire（覆盖），本义是把盖子揭开。

items.en: Cooperire meant to cover something completely.
items.cn: cooperire 指把东西完全盖住。

items.en: Dis- undid that cover, so the thing stood bare.
items.cn: 前缀 dis- 把覆盖去掉，东西就露了出来。

items.en: Descovrir meant to uncover or lay bare.
items.cn: 古法语 descovrir 指揭开覆盖、露出本来面目。

items.en: English took it as to reveal or find out.
items.cn: 英语借入时表示揭露或查明。

items.en: The word now covers a lucky find and a slow research.
items.cn: 今天它既指偶然碰上，也指长期研究所得。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the cover stem, and the meaning group lists other ways of finding.
note.cn: 形近组保留 cover 这段词干，近义组列出别的表示找到的词。

entries.definition: to put something over another thing
entries.definitionCN: 把东西盖在另一物上

entries.definition: to remove a cover or bring to light
entries.definitionCN: 揭开覆盖或使显露

entries.definition: the act or result of finding
entries.definitionCN: 发现的行为或结果

entries.definition: to come upon something by chance or search
entries.definitionCN: 偶然或搜寻中碰到

entries.definition: to notice something hidden or faint
entries.definitionCN: 察觉隐蔽或微弱之物

entries.definition: to see something suddenly
entries.definitionCN: 突然看见

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a lifted cover and end with a fact that fits into place.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从揭开的盖子开始，落到终于对上位置的一件事。

normal.en: Dis- plus cover: take the cover off.

normal.en: A child discovers a beetle under a stone.

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 discover 记成「揭开盖子」：dis 是去掉，cover 是盖子，盖子一揭，藏着的东西就露出来。

senses.title: A difference between things that should match
senses.titleCN: 本应相符之物出现差异
senses.definition: a difference between two facts, figures or accounts that are expected to agree
senses.definitionCN: 本应一致的两项事实、数字或记录之间出现的差别
senses.example: Auditors found a discrepancy between the two ledgers.
senses.exampleCN: 审计人员发现两本账簿之间有出入。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to sound discordantly, so a discrepancy is two records refusing to sound alike.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「响声不谐」，因此差异就是两份记录的声音对不上。

senses.title: An accounting difference
senses.definition: a difference in a bookkeeping entry that prevents the books from balancing
senses.definitionCN: 使账目不平的一处记账差别
senses.example: A discrepancy of two hundred units delayed the audit.
senses.exampleCN: 一笔两百单位的差额拖慢了审计。
senses.why: A ledger is a set of figures that must agree, and any figure that does not add up is flagged by this word.
senses.whyCN: 账簿是一组必须对上的数字，任何加不平的数字都用这个词标出。

senses.title: A measurement difference
senses.definition: a difference between two measurements of the same quantity
senses.definitionCN: 同一数量两次测量之间出现的差别
senses.example: The discrepancy between the two instruments pointed to a loose sensor.
senses.exampleCN: 两台仪器之间的测量差异指向一个松动的传感器。
senses.why: Two instruments aimed at one quantity should read alike, so their disagreement is itself evidence.
senses.whyCN: 两台仪器测同一个量本应读数相同，因此它们的不一致本身就是证据。

senses.title: A gap between theory and data
senses.definition: a difference between what a model predicts and what is observed
senses.definitionCN: 模型预测与观测结果之间的差别
senses.example: The discrepancy between prediction and observation forced a revision.
senses.exampleCN: 预测与观测之间的差距迫使研究修改。
senses.why: Science advances when a model's promise and nature's answer fail to agree.
senses.whyCN: 当模型的承诺与自然的回答对不上时，科学才向前走。

senses.title: A gap between promise and practice
senses.definition: a difference between what is announced and what is actually done
senses.definitionCN: 宣布的内容与实际所做之事之间的差别
senses.example: The discrepancy between the policy and its enforcement was obvious.
senses.exampleCN: 政策与其执行之间的不一致一目了然。
senses.why: Words and deeds are two records of the same intention, and the word reports that they do not match.
senses.whyCN: 言辞与行动是同一个意图的两份记录，这个词报告两者对不上。

senses.title: An audit or statistical discrepancy
senses.definition: a mismatch uncovered by checking records against one another or against counts
senses.definitionCN: 把记录互相核对或与清点结果核对时发现的不符
senses.example: The census reported a discrepancy in two districts.
senses.exampleCN: 人口普查报告了两个辖区的一处出入。
senses.why: Counting twice is the oldest audit, and any gap between the two counts needs a name.
senses.whyCN: 数两遍是最古老的审计，两次清点之间的缺口需要一个名称。

senses.title: A difference between accounts of an event
senses.definition: a difference between two people's versions of the same event
senses.definitionCN: 两人对同一事件的叙述之间出现的差别
senses.example: The discrepancy between the two witnesses puzzled the court.
senses.exampleCN: 两名证人陈述之间的差异让法庭困惑。
senses.why: Two observers of one event should tell one story, and their divergence is what courts must resolve.
senses.whyCN: 同一件事的两名观察者本应讲出一个版本，他们的分歧正是法庭要解决的。

senses.title: A discrepancy in replication
senses.definition: a failure of a second experiment to reproduce the first result
senses.definitionCN: 第二次实验未能再现第一次结果
senses.example: The discrepancy between the two trials raised doubts about the finding.
senses.exampleCN: 两次试验之间的不一致使人们对结论产生怀疑。
senses.why: Replication is a second record of the same effect, and a mismatch weakens the first claim.
senses.whyCN: 重复实验是同一效应的第二份记录，对不上就削弱了第一个结论。

intro.en: Discrepancy comes from Latin discrepantia, discordance, from discrepare, to sound discordantly, built from dis-, apart, and crepare, to rattle or creak. English took the noun in the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 discrepantia「不和谐」，源头是动词 discrepare「响声不和」，由表示「分开」的前缀与表示「嘎嘎作响」的词根构成。英语在十七世纪借入这个名词。

items.en: The verb meant to rattle, creak or make a noise, and it also stands behind decrepit.
items.cn: 这个动词意为嘎嘎作响、吱嘎出声，也是「破旧」一词的源头。

items.en: The prefix meant apart or in different directions.
items.cn: 这个前缀意为分开、朝不同方向。

items.en: The compound meant to sound out of tune with one another.
items.cn: 这个复合动词意为彼此的声音不合调。

items.en: The noun named the state of not agreeing, first of sounds and then of facts.
items.cn: 这个名词指不一致的状态，先用于声音，后用于事实。

items.en: French carried the noun into English, where it named mismatches in records and accounts.
items.cn: 法语把这个名词带进英语，用于指记录与账目中的不符。

items.en: Later usage extended it to measurements, statistics, testimony and replication.
items.cn: 后来的用法把它扩展到测量、统计、证词与重复实验。

note.en: The first group shares the root or the noun ending; the second group names other kinds of difference.
note.cn: 第一组共享词根或名词词尾；第二组是其他表示差异的说法。

entries.definition: The adjective for things that do not agree.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指不一致的。

entries.definition: In a manner that does not agree.
entries.definitionCN: 指以不一致的方式。

entries.definition: Separate and distinct; close in spelling but from another Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 分开而独立；拼写相近，但来自另一个拉丁动词。

entries.definition: Careful judgement or freedom to decide; a different Latin verb behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 谨慎判断或自行决定的自由；背后是另一个拉丁动词。

entries.definition: Worn out, from the same verb of creaking.
entries.definitionCN: 指破旧的，出自同一个「吱嘎作响」动词。

entries.definition: The general word for two things not being the same.
entries.definitionCN: 指两物不相同的一般说法。

entries.definition: A failure to stay the same from one case to the next.
entries.definitionCN: 指前后未能保持一致。

entries.definition: A difference in level or condition, often unfair.
entries.definitionCN: 指水平或状况上的差距，常带不公平意味。

entries.definition: A change or difference within a range.
entries.definitionCN: 指范围内出现的变化或差异。

entries.definition: An empty space or a shortfall between two points.
entries.definitionCN: 指空缺或两点之间的落差。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the Latin image of sounds that will not agree, then apply it to books, instruments and testimony.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着拉丁语中「声音合不到一起」的意象，再把它用到账簿、仪器与证词上。

normal.en: The root verb means to creak, so a discrepancy is two records creaking out of tune.
normal.cn: 词根意为嘎嘎作响，所以差异就是两份记录的响声不合调。

normal.en: Auditors look for a discrepancy between the ledger and the count.
normal.cn: 审计人员找的是账簿与清点结果之间的出入。

normal.en: Two instruments measuring the same thing should agree, and their discrepancy points to a fault.
normal.cn: 两台仪器测同一件事本应一致，它们的差异指向某个故障。

normal.en: A model that predicts one value while observation gives another has a discrepancy to explain.
normal.cn: 模型预测一个值、观测给出另一个值，就有差异需要解释。

normal.en: Two witnesses telling different stories create a discrepancy for the court.
normal.cn: 两名证人讲出不同版本，就给法庭造成一处不一致。

abstract.en: A discrepancy is a place where two truths refuse to sit on the same line.
abstract.cn: 差异是两个真相不肯坐进同一条线的地方。

abstract.en: Records are promises to agree, and the word reports a broken promise.
abstract.cn: 记录是「应当一致」的承诺，这个词报告承诺被违背。

abstract.en: What cannot be made to agree can still be made to explain, which is where research begins.
abstract.cn: 无法被凑成一致的东西仍可被解释，研究就从这里开始。

examples.en: The discrepancy between the invoice and the order delayed payment.
examples.cn: 发票与订单之间的出入拖慢了付款。

examples.en: A discrepancy in the two measurements suggested a faulty gauge.
examples.cn: 两次测量间的差异表明仪表有故障。

examples.en: The committee asked the agency to explain the discrepancy in its figures.
examples.cn: 委员会要求该机构解释数字上的出入。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「迪斯克瑞彭西」——两本账对不上，嘎嘎响不到一个调上，就是「差异、不一致」：差异、出入

root: 来自拉丁语 discrepantia「不和谐」，源头 discrepare「响声不和」，由 dis-「分开」与 crepare「嘎嘎作响」构成；英语在十七世纪借入，后扩展到测量、统计、证词与重复实验。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses trace a mismatch through records, accounts, instruments, models, promises, audits, testimony and replication.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把「对不上」追到记录、账目、仪器、模型、承诺、审计、证词与重复实验。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two ledgers open on one desk, the same expense written in two different figures.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一张桌上两本摊开的账簿，同一笔支出写着两个不同数字。

branches.en: THE TWO VERSIONS: records and testimony fail to agree on one event.
branches.cn: 两个版本：记录与证词在同一件事上对不上。

branches.en: THE BOOKS AND THE COUNT: an audit finds figures that will not balance.
branches.cn: 账簿与清点：审计发现数字无法轧平。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENTS DISAGREE: two measurements of one quantity differ.
branches.cn: 仪器不一致：同一数量的两次测量出现差别。

branches.en: THE PREDICTION AND THE REPEAT: a model misses the data, and a second trial misses the first.
branches.cn: 预测与重复：模型对不上数据，第二次试验对不上第一次。

branches.en: THE PROMISE AND THE PRACTICE: what is announced is not what is done.
branches.cn: 承诺与做法：宣布的内容并非实际所做。

intro.en: The word is built on a Latin verb of harsh sound, so its core image is two things out of tune.
intro.cn: 这个词建在表示「刺耳声响」的拉丁动词上，核心意象是两样东西不合调。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the verb of creaking, the prefix of separation, the compound verb and the noun of discord.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了表示吱嘎作响的动词、表示分开的前缀、复合动词与表示不谐的名词。

items.example: The root supplies the noise image.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供声响意象。

items.example: It makes two sounds go apart.
The verb is the source of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是英语名词的源头。

items.example: The noun named the state of disagreement.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指不一致的状态。

items.example: English applied it to accounts and data.
items.exampleCN: 英语把它用于账目与数据。

items.example: The adjective adds a Latin ending.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词加了拉丁词尾。
它标记类似分词的形容词。

items.example: A related word from the same verb of creaking.
items.exampleCN: 出自同一个「吱嘎」动词的相关词。

derivatives.zh: 加形容词词尾构成，义为「不一致的」
加副词词尾构成，义为「以不一致方式」
由拉丁名词经法语进入英语，义为「差异」
该名词的复数，义为「多处不一致」

definition_zh: 谨慎；判断力；自行裁量的自由
definition_en: the quality of judging wisely, and the freedom to act on that judgement
core_image: 一位老管家站在宴会厅门口，把该说的话咽回去，把该放的人放进去，手一直按在门把上
scene: 宴会厅门口有人争执起来，管家没有立刻表态。The steward left the seating to her discretion.
sceneCN: 这里 discretion 指依自己的判断作决定的自由（第 2 个义项：自行裁量）；句意为管家让她自行安排座位。

senses.title: Ability to judge wisely
senses.definition: the quality of seeing what a situation calls for and acting accordingly
senses.definitionCN: 看清情势所需并据此行事的能力
senses.example: She handled the quarrel with great discretion.
senses.exampleCN: 她极为明智地处理了那场争吵。
senses.why: The word names a kind of judgement that shows itself in the timing of action and silence.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的判断力，体现在行动与沉默的时机上。

senses.title: Freedom to decide
senses.definition: the power to choose how to act without being told by another
senses.definitionCN: 不受他人指派而自行选择行动方式的权力
senses.example: The steward left the seating to her discretion.
senses.exampleCN: 管家让她自行安排座位。
senses.why: Discretion here is a grant of space: someone hands you the decision instead of a rule.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 discretion 是一种空间授予：别人把决定交给你，而不是给你一条规则。

senses.title: Formal right to choose
senses.definition: a legal or official right to decide within set limits
senses.definitionCN: 在既定范围内作出决定的法律或官方权利
senses.example: The trustee may sell the land at his discretion.
senses.exampleCN: 受托人可自行决定出售这块土地。
senses.why: In law the word defines a bounded freedom: the holder chooses, but only inside the granted scope.
senses.whyCN: 在法律中，这个词界定一种有边界的自由：持有者可以选，但只在被授予的范围内。

senses.title: Habit of keeping quiet
senses.definition: the practice of not revealing what one knows about others
senses.definitionCN: 不泄露自己所知的他人私事的习惯
senses.example: He told the secret to no one, and his discretion was admired.
senses.exampleCN: 他没把秘密告诉任何人，这份守口如瓶令人称道。
senses.why: Silence is often the clearest proof of discretion, because nothing said cannot be repeated.
senses.whyCN: 沉默常是谨慎最清楚的证明，因为没说出口的话无法被复述。

senses.title: Tact in choosing words
senses.definition: care in speech so that nothing needlessly wounds or exposes
senses.definitionCN: 说话时避免无谓伤人、揭短的分寸
senses.example: She described the failure with discretion, sparing the young man's name.
senses.exampleCN: 她得体地描述这次失败，没有点出那个年轻人的名字。
senses.why: Tact is discretion applied to language: the same fact, told in a way that protects.
senses.whyCN: 得体是用于语言的谨慎：同一件事，用保护人的方式说出来。

senses.title: The age of reason
senses.definition: the age at which a child is treated as able to judge right from wrong
senses.definitionCN: 孩子被视为能分辨是非的年龄
senses.example: The court found that he had reached the age of discretion.
senses.exampleCN: 法院认定他已到了懂事年龄。
senses.why: The phrase turns judgement into a threshold: past a certain age, one is held responsible for it.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法把判断力变成一道门槛：过了某个年龄，就要为自己的判断负责。

senses.title: Latitude within the law
senses.definition: the room a judge or official has to interpret rules case by case
senses.definitionCN: 法官或官员逐案解释规则时拥有的余地
senses.example: The sentence fell within the judge's discretion.
senses.exampleCN: 这一判决在法官的裁量范围内。
senses.why: Rules cannot cover every case, so the system deliberately leaves a pocket of choice.
senses.whyCN: 规则无法覆盖每个案子，于是制度故意留下一个可选择的口袋。

senses.title: Keeping something private
senses.definition: the state of being kept from public knowledge by choice
senses.definitionCN: 因选择而不让公众知晓的状态
senses.example: The details were handled with discretion and never reached the press.
senses.exampleCN: 细节被谨慎处理，从未传到媒体。
senses.why: Here discretion is not a person's skill but an outcome: information stays inside a closed circle.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 discretion 不是个人技能，而是一种结果：信息留在封闭的圈子里。

intro.en: Discretion comes from a Latin verb for sifting apart, and the image of separating good from bad still sits inside it.
intro.cn: discretion 来自一个表示「分开筛拣」的拉丁动词，把好坏分开的画面至今仍在词里。

items.en: English took the noun from Old French in the 14c., first as a word for discernment.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪从古法语借入这个名词，最初指辨别力。

items.en: Old French discrecion meant 'judgement, prudence', the practical side of discernment.
items.cn: 古法语 discrecion 意为「判断、审慎」，是辨别力中偏实践的一面。

items.en: Late Latin discretio meant 'a separating, a distinction', like sifting grain from chaff.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 discretio 意为「分开、区分」，像把谷粒从糠里筛出来。

items.en: Cernere 'to sift, to separate' is the root; the same root gives discern and discriminate.
items.cn: cernere「筛、分」是词根；同一词根还给出 discern 与 discriminate。

items.en: Modern usage adds a legal sense: the bounded freedom an official has to choose.
items.cn: 现代用法又添了法律义：官员拥有的一种有边界的自由。

note.en: The look-alike group turns on one letter that separates two very different words; the near-meaning group names neighbouring virtues.
note.cn: 形近组的关键只在一个字母，却分出两个差别很大的词；近义组列出相邻的美德。

entries.definition: careful not to reveal private matters.
entries.definitionCN: 小心不泄露私事的。

entries.definition: separate and distinct, not continuous.
entries.definitionCN: 分开而独立的，不连续的。

entries.definition: left to one's own judgement.
entries.definitionCN: 由本人判断决定的。

entries.definition: in a careful, quiet manner.
entries.definitionCN: 谨慎而低调地。

entries.definition: good judgement about risks before acting.
entries.definitionCN: 行动前对风险的明智判断。

entries.definition: the ability to say difficult things without giving offence.
entries.definitionCN: 把难说的话说得不得罪人的能力。

entries.definition: the amount of freedom allowed in a decision.
entries.definitionCN: 决定时被允许的自由幅度。

entries.definition: care taken to avoid danger or error.
entries.definitionCN: 为避免危险或错误而采取的谨慎。

normalIntro.en: The hooks hold on to the picture of a hand resting on a door handle, deciding who may pass.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把「一只手放在门把上、决定谁能通过」的画面留住。

normal.en: Discretion contains crest: a wise person keeps a cool crest above the crowd.
normal.cn: discretion 里有 crest（ crest 山脊）：明智的人能站在高处看清全局。

normal.en: Discreet and discrete differ by the t in the middle: keep the t for the careful one.
normal.cn: discreet 与 discrete 只差中间两个字母的位置：谨慎的那个保留 e 在末尾。

normal.en: Think of a doorman who lets the right people in and keeps the secret out.
normal.cn: 想象一个门房，放对的人进来，把秘密关在门外。

normal.en: Say dis-KRESH-un; the stressed syllable sounds like a hushed decision.
normal.cn: 读成 dis-KRESH-un，重读音节听起来像一次压低声音的决定。

normal.en: Pair it with judgement: discretion is judgement with a door in its hand.
normal.cn: 把它和 judgement 配对：discretion 是手里握着门的判断力。

abstract.en: Freedom and care live in the same word because a good decision needs both.
abstract.cn: 自由与谨慎住在同一个词里，因为好的决定两者都需要。

abstract.en: What is left unsaid is often the strongest exercise of discretion.
abstract.cn: 没有说出口的话，常常是谨慎最有力的行使。

abstract.en: Every rule leaves a small pocket of choice; that pocket is discretion.
abstract.cn: 每条规则都留下一个小小的选择口袋，那个口袋就是裁量。

examples.en: She handled the quarrel with great discretion.
examples.cn: 她极为明智地处理了那场争吵。

examples.en: The steward left the seating to her discretion.
examples.cn: 管家让她自行安排座位。

examples.en: The details were handled with discretion and never reached the press.
examples.cn: 细节被谨慎处理，从未传到媒体。

dict_mnemonic.text: dis（分开）+ cret（筛）+ ion（名词）：把该说的与该藏的筛开，就是「谨慎、裁量」。

root: 拉丁语 cernere（筛、分）→ discretio（区分），经古法语 discrecion 进入英语

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses grow from one act: separating what fits from what does not, then choosing inside that cleared space.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从一个动作长出来：把合宜的与不合宜的分开，然后在这块清出来的空间里作选择。

core.en: SEPARATING THEN CHOOSING
core.cn: 先分开，再选择

branches.en: The inner skill of judging and the tact that shows it in speech.
branches.cn: 内在的判断力，以及在言语中体现它的得体。

branches.en: Freedom granted by a person, a contract or a court.
branches.cn: 由人、契约或法院授予的自由。

branches.en: Silence that protects a secret from being repeated.
branches.cn: 保护秘密不被复述的沉默。

branches.en: The age at which judgement becomes a legal duty.
branches.cn: 判断力成为法律义务的那个年龄。

branches.en: The same word names the skill and the room to use it.
branches.cn: 同一个词既命名技能，也命名使用技能的空间。

intro.en: The family splits into two spellings: discreet for the careful person, discrete for the separate thing, and discretion holding both ideas.
intro.cn: 这个词族分成两种拼法：discreet 指谨慎的人，discrete 指分开的事物，而 discretion 同时握住这两个念头。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root cernere means to sift, and its past participle cretus gives the noun its shape.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 cernere 意为筛，其过去分词 cretus 给了名词现在的形状。

items.meaning: a sifting apart, then a judgement
items.meaningCN: 分开筛拣，而后作出判断

items.example: He was discreet about the visit.
items.exampleCN: 他对这次拜访守口如瓶。

items.meaningCN: 被分成各自独立的部分
items.example: The plot has three discrete stages.
items.exampleCN: 这个情节有三个独立阶段。

items.example: She could discern a change in his voice.
items.exampleCN: 她能辨出他声音里的变化。
他的辨别力救了这个项目。

items.meaning: to draw a line between things
items.example: The test discriminates between close answers.
items.exampleCN: 这项测试能区分接近的答案。

items.meaning: to set apart and hide away
items.example: The gland secretes a thin fluid.
items.exampleCN: 这个腺体分泌一种稀薄的液体。

items.example: One thing is certain: the door was locked.
items.exampleCN: 有一件事是确定的：门是锁着的。

definition_zh: 区分；辨别；歧视；区别对待
definition_en: to perceive a difference between things, or to treat people unequally because of their group
core_image: 用筛子把大小不同的颗粒分开
scene: 招聘会上，面试官翻着一份简历，年龄栏被红笔圈起。 At the job fair the interviewer discriminated against an applicant because of her age.
sceneCN: 这里 discriminate 是「歧视」（第 4 个义项：因群体身份而不公平对待）；句意：招聘会上，面试官因为年龄而歧视一位应聘者。

collocations.zh: 把 A 与 B 区分开

senses.title: Perceive a difference
senses.definition: to notice that two things are different
senses.definitionCN: 注意到两件事物不同
senses.example: Babies can discriminate between familiar and new faces.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿能分辨熟悉与陌生的面孔。
senses.why: Latin discriminare means 'to divide, separate', from discrimen 'distinction'. The first English sense, 1620s, is the mental act of marking that division.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 discriminare 意为“分开、分离”，来自 discrimen“区别”。英语最早义（17 世纪 20 年代）就是在心里标记这条分界。

senses.title: Distinguish one thing from another
senses.titleCN: 把一物与另一物区分开
senses.definition: to recognize the difference between two specific things
senses.definitionCN: 认出两个具体事物之间的差异
senses.example: Readers must discriminate fact from opinion.
senses.exampleCN: 读者必须把事实与观点区分开。
senses.why: The verb takes two objects because the line is drawn between them. discrimen is the interval or mark between two things, so discrimination is always relational.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词带两个宾语，因为线是在两者之间画的。discrimen 就是两物之间的间隔或标记，所以“区分”总是关系性的。

senses.title: Show fine judgment or taste
senses.definition: to show the ability to make careful distinctions, especially in quality
senses.definitionCN: 表现出仔细辨别、尤指辨别品质的能力
senses.example: She has a discriminating palate for wine.
senses.exampleCN: 她对葡萄酒有敏锐的鉴别力。
senses.why: The adjective discriminating (1792) is the positive side of the same skill. A person who can sift fine differences is said to have taste, not prejudice.
senses.whyCN: 形容词 discriminating（1792）是同一能力的正面面。能筛出细微差异的人被说成品味好，而不是有偏见。

senses.title: Treat people unequally
senses.definition: to treat people differently and unfairly because of their group
senses.definitionCN: 因所属群体而不公平地对待人
senses.example: It is illegal to discriminate by age.
senses.exampleCN: 因年龄歧视是违法的。
senses.why: The adverse sense, 'make invidious distinctions prejudicial to a class of persons', is first recorded in 1866 in American English. The neutral line-drawing turns into a hierarchy.
senses.whyCN: 负面义“对某类人作出有害区分”最早记录于 1866 年的美国英语。中性的画线变成了等级。

senses.title: Discriminate against someone
senses.definition: to deny someone opportunities or fair treatment because of who they are
senses.definitionCN: 因某人的身份而剥夺机会或公平待遇
senses.example: The firm was accused of discriminating against women.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司被指控歧视女性。
senses.why: The fixed pattern discriminate against makes the target explicit. The verb now names an action with a victim, not merely a perception.
senses.whyCN: 固定搭配 discriminate against 明确点出受害者。这个动词现在指带有受害者的行为，而不只是感知。

senses.title: Separate signals from noise
senses.definition: in electronics, to select wanted signals and reject unwanted ones
senses.definitionCN: 电子学中选出所需信号、排除干扰
senses.example: The circuit discriminates noise from signal.
senses.exampleCN: 这个电路能鉴别噪声与信号。
senses.why: Engineering keeps the original 'sift' image almost literally: a circuit separates one kind of input from another and passes only the wanted kind.
senses.whyCN: 工程学几乎字面保留了“筛”的意象：电路把一类输入与另一类分开，只放行所需的一类。

senses.title: Apply a discriminatory rule
senses.definition: to operate a rule or practice that disadvantages a protected group
senses.definitionCN: 执行使受保护群体处于不利地位的规则或做法
senses.example: Landlords may not discriminate against tenants with children.
senses.exampleCN: 房东不得歧视带孩子的租户。
senses.why: Legal usage turns the verb into a name for a prohibited practice. The distinction is no longer neutral; the law defines which lines may not be drawn.
senses.whyCN: 法律用法把这个动词变成对禁止行为的称呼。区分不再中性；法律界定哪些线不得画。

senses.title: Distinct, marked off (archaic adjective)
senses.titleCN: 独特的；被区分开的（古形容词）
senses.definition: in 17c. use, an adjective meaning 'distinct'
senses.definitionCN: 在 17 世纪用法中作形容词，意为“独特的”
senses.example: In 17c. texts a discriminate difference meant a clearly marked one.
senses.exampleCN: 在 17 世纪文本中，a discriminate difference 指被清楚标出的差异。
senses.why: The adjective sense, recorded 1620s, meant 'distinct'; the later sense 'perceiving nice differences' is from 1798. It survives mainly inside discriminating and indiscriminate.
senses.whyCN: 形容词义记录于 17 世纪 20 年代，意为“独特的”；后来“能察觉细微差异”的义项始于 1798 年。它主要残留在 discriminating 与 indiscriminate 中。

intro.en: Discriminate began as a neutral act of separating, then acquired one of the strongest social meanings in English. The root cernere 'to sift' explains both the neutral and the contested senses.
intro.cn: discriminate 起初是中性的“分开”动作，后来获得英语中最强烈的社会含义之一。词根 cernere“筛”解释了它的中性义与争议义。

items.en: The verb means 'distinguish from something else or from each other, observe or mark the differences'.
items.cn: 动词义为“把某物与别物区分开，或观察并标记差异”。

items.en: From discriminatus, past participle of discriminare 'to divide, separate', from discrimen 'interval, distinction'.
items.cn: 来自 discriminatus，即 discriminare“分开、分离”的过去分词，源头是 discrimen“间隔、区别”。

items.en: discrimen derives from discernere 'to separate, sift, distinguish', from dis- 'off, away' + cernere 'sift' (PIE *krei- 'to sieve').
items.cn: discrimen 来自 discernere“分开、筛、辨别”，由 dis-“离开”+ cernere“筛”（原始印欧语 *krei-“筛”）。

items.en: An adjective sense 'distinct' is recorded; the sense 'perceiving nice differences' is from 1798.
items.cn: 形容词义“独特的”被记录；“能察觉细微差异”的义项始于 1798 年。

items.en: discriminating 'possessing discernment' appears, the positive side of the same skill.
items.cn: discriminating“有辨别力的”出现，是同一能力的正面面。

items.en: The adverse sense 'make invidious distinctions prejudicial to a class of persons' is first recorded in American English.
items.cn: 负面义“对某类人作出有害区分”最早记录于美国英语。

note.en: The first group is about forms in the same family; the second is about verbs that also tell things apart.
note.cn: 第一组看同一词族的形态，第二组看同样把事物区分开的动词。

entries.definition: showing careful judgment and good taste; the positive sense of the skill.
entries.definitionCN: 有鉴别力的；品味好的（该能力的正面义）。

entries.definition: unfairly treating a group; the negative institutional sense.
entries.definitionCN: 歧视性的；不公平对待群体的（负面的制度义）。

entries.definition: done without choosing carefully; random or widespread.
entries.definitionCN: 不加区分的；随意的（in- 表否定）。

entries.definition: to see or show a difference, often with careful attention. It is neutral and broad.
entries.definitionCN: 看出或表明差异，常含仔细留意。它中性而宽泛。

entries.definition: to make or recognize a difference, especially in a technical or systematic way.
entries.definitionCN: 使不同或认出差异，尤指技术性、系统性地。

entries.definition: to perceive something with difficulty or subtlety. It stresses the effort of seeing.
entries.definitionCN: 费力或细微地察觉某物。它强调“看见”的努力。

normalIntro.en: Real links: the root cernere 'sift', the 1866 social sense, the positive discriminating, and the legal pattern discriminate against.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：词根 cernere“筛”、1866 年的社会义、正面的 discriminating，以及法律搭配 discriminate against。

normal.en: The root cernere means 'to sift'. To discriminate is to pass things through a sieve and keep the wanted grains.
normal.cn: 词根 cernere 意为“筛”。discriminate 就是把东西过筛，留下想要的颗粒。

normal.en: discrimen is the interval between two things; a distinction exists only where two items meet.
normal.cn: discrimen 是两物之间的间隔；只有两物相遇之处才有区分。

normal.en: discriminating taste is the same sieve used well: fine differences are kept, coarse ones rejected.
normal.cn: discriminating taste 就是使用得当的同一张筛子：留下细微差异，筛掉粗糙之处。

normal.en: In 1866 American English the neutral sieve became a hierarchy: some people were sorted out and denied fair treatment.
normal.cn: 1866 年美国英语中，中性的筛子变成了等级：一些人被筛出去，失去公平待遇。

normal.en: The legal pattern discriminate against names a victim, which is why it is the strongest use of the word.
normal.cn: 法律搭配 discriminate against 点明受害者，因此是这个词语气最强的用法。

abstract.en: Discrimination is selection: every sieve includes and excludes at once. The ethics lie in who chose the mesh.
abstract.cn: 区分就是选择：每张筛子都同时容纳与排除。伦理在于是谁选了筛孔。

abstract.en: The word holds both discernment and prejudice because both are acts of sorting; only the purpose separates them.
abstract.cn: 这个词同时容纳“鉴别力”与“偏见”，因为两者都是分拣动作；区分它们的是目的。

abstract.en: A just distinction marks differences without using them to deny a share; an unjust one turns a difference into a rank.
abstract.cn: 公正的区分标出差异却不借此剥夺份额；不公正的区分把差异变成等级。

examples.en: Babies can discriminate between familiar and new faces.
examples.cn: 婴儿能分辨熟悉与陌生的面孔。

examples.en: It is illegal to discriminate by age.
examples.cn: 因年龄歧视是违法的。

examples.en: Readers must discriminate fact from opinion.
examples.cn: 读者必须把事实与观点区分开。

dict_mnemonic.text: “地是亏米”——地里的米亏了，要筛一筛分开好坏 → discriminate 区分、歧视

root: 拉丁语 discriminare“分开、分离”，来自 discrimen“区别”，再上为 discernere“筛、辨别”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of discriminate, all built on one act: sifting. Sifting can be neutral (telling kinds apart), skilled (good taste), technical (separating signal from noise), or unjust (denying a group fair treatment).
sensesIntro.cn: discriminate 的八个义项都建立在一个动作上：筛。筛可以是中性的（分出种类）、有技巧的（好品味）、技术的（分离信号与噪声），或是不义的（剥夺某群体的公平待遇）。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sieve separating grains of different sizes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张筛子把大小不同的颗粒分开。

branches.en: SEPARATE: the neutral core, drawing a line between two kinds and telling them apart.
branches.cn: 分开：中性核心，在两类之间画线并把它们辨开。

branches.en: MARKED OFF: the old adjective describes the thing that has been separated and stands distinct.
branches.cn: 被标出：旧形容词描述已被分开、独自成立之物。

branches.en: QUALITY: the same sieve used with skill produces discriminating taste.
branches.cn: 品质：同一张筛子用得娴熟，就产生有鉴别力的品味。

branches.en: PREJUDICE: the line becomes a hierarchy and denies fair treatment.
branches.cn: 偏见：线变成等级，剥夺公平待遇。

branches.en: SIGNAL: engineering keeps the literal sieve, passing one kind of input only.
branches.cn: 信号：工程学保留字面的筛，只放行一类输入。

intro.en: Discriminate is built on the Latin stem discrimin-. English adds -tion, -tory, -ting, -tive, -able, and the negative prefixes in- and non-.
intro.cn: discriminate 建立在拉丁词干 discrimin- 上。英语加 -tion、-tory、-ting、-tive、-able，以及否定前缀 in-、non-。

latinIntro.en: Latin discriminare, discrimen, and discernere all belong to the 'sift' family. Cernere 'to sift' also underlies discern, secret, and certain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 discriminare、discrimen、discernere 都属于“筛”的词族。cernere“筛”也是 discern、secret、certain 的深层来源。

having been distinguished or treated unfairly

definition_zh: 歧视；辨别力
definition_en: unfair treatment of a group of people, or the ability to see fine differences
core_image: 两张几乎一样的简历被推向桌子两边，一边的椅子却更高
scene: 两叠简历内容几乎一样，却被推向了不同的方向。She spoke out against discrimination in hiring.

senses.title: Unfair treatment of a group
senses.definition: the unfair treatment of people because of their group, age or sex
senses.definitionCN: 因所属群体、年龄或性别而受到的不公平对待
senses.example: The law forbids discrimination at work.
senses.exampleCN: 法律禁止职场歧视。
senses.why: A line is drawn first, and then one side is given less.
senses.whyCN: 先画一道线，然后让一边少拿。

senses.title: The power to tell things apart
senses.definition: the ability to see small differences between things
senses.definitionCN: 看出事物之间细微差别的能力
senses.example: Good tea needs a fine discrimination of smell.
senses.exampleCN: 懂好茶需要精细的嗅觉辨别力。
senses.why: The same sharp eye that separates can also sort people unfairly.
senses.whyCN: 能分辨的锐利眼光，也可能被用来不公平地分流人群。

intro.en: Discrimination comes from Latin discriminare, to divide or separate, from discrimen, a dividing line.
intro.cn: discrimination 来自拉丁语 discriminare（分开、区分），其根 discrimen 指分界线。

items.en: Discrimen meant a line that separates two things.
items.cn: discrimen 指把两样东西分开的界线。

items.en: Discriminare meant to divide or to distinguish.
items.cn: discriminare 指划分或加以区别。

items.en: English used it for the act of telling differences.
items.cn: 英语借入后指辨别差异的行为。

items.en: The sense of unfair treatment by group grew in law and politics.
items.cn: 按群体不公平对待这一义项在法律与政治中长出来。

items.en: Both the sharp eye and the closed door keep the same word.
items.cn: 敏锐的眼光与关上的门，共用这一个词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the discrimin- stem, and the meaning group names unfair attitudes.
note.cn: 形近组共享 discrimin- 词干，近义组列出几种不公平的态度。

entries.definition: to see a difference or to treat unfairly
entries.definitionCN: 分辨差异或加以不公平对待

entries.definition: able to judge fine differences
entries.definitionCN: 能分辨细微差别的

entries.definition: done without any choice or care
entries.definitionCN: 不加选择、不加分辨的

entries.definition: a leaning that makes judgement unfair
entries.definitionCN: 使判断不公的偏向

entries.definition: an opinion formed before the facts

entries.definition: the quality of not being just

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a chalk line and end with a hand that can weigh two shades.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一道粉笔线开始，落到一只能掂量两种色差的手。

normal.en: Discrimin- means to separate; -ion makes it a practice.
normal.cn: discrimin- 是分开，-ion 把它变成一种做法。

normal.en: A line drawn around a group soon becomes a wall.
normal.cn: 围着某个群体画下的线，很快会变成墙。

normal.en: The same word praises a fine palate and blames a closed door.
normal.cn: 同一个词既夸精细的品味，也指责关上的门。

normal.en: Discrimination at work can hide inside a polite rule.
normal.cn: 职场歧视能藏在一条规定里。

normal.en: A discriminating reader notices the missing sentence.

abstract.en: Picture one line of chalk across a table.
abstract.cn: 想象桌面上划过一道粉笔线。

abstract.en: Picture two identical files placed at different heights.
abstract.cn: 想象两份一样的档案被放在不同高度。

abstract.en: Picture an eye that can weigh two almost equal colours.
abstract.cn: 想象一只眼能掂量两种几乎相同的颜色。

examples.en: The company was sued for discrimination.
examples.cn: 这家公司因歧视被起诉。

examples.en: She has a fine discrimination of taste and smell.
examples.cn: 她对味道与气味有精细的辨别力。

examples.en: Age discrimination is hard to prove.
examples.cn: 年龄歧视很难证明。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 discrimination 记成「划线分开」：discrimin- 是划分，-ion 是行为；把人按群体划开并少给，就是歧视；把事物细细划开，就是辨别力。

root: 源自拉丁语 discrimen（分界线）与 discriminare（划分、区别），进入英语后先指辨别差异，十九世纪起在法律与政治语境里指按群体给予不公平对待，于是同一个词兼有「辨别力」与「歧视」两面。

sensesIntro.en: From the act of drawing a line between things, to the unfair line drawn around people.
sensesIntro.cn: 从在事物之间划线，到围着人群划出的一条不公平的线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chalk line across a table, with one side quietly given less.

definition_en: the feeling that someone or something is unworthy of respect; to treat as unworthy
core_image: 一个人从上往下斜眼看递过来的东西，手背一翻把它推开；下巴抬得比对方头顶还高

senses.why: A closed mouth beside an outstretched hand.
senses.whyCN: 一张闭紧的嘴旁边伸着一只手。

intro.en: Disdain is dis- plus the root of deign; it comes from Old French desdignier, from Latin dignari, to deem worthy, from dignus, worthy, so it means not even deigning.
intro.cn: disdain 由 dis-（否定）加 deign（屈尊）的词根构成；它来自古法语 desdignier，上溯拉丁语 dignari「认为值得」，词根 dignus「值得的」，字面是「连屈尊都不肯」。

items.en: Latin dignus means worthy or deserving.
items.cn: 拉丁语 dignus 意为值得的、配得上的。

items.en: Dignari meant to deem something worthy.
items.cn: dignari 意为认为某事值得。

items.en: Old French desdignier meant to scorn as unworthy.
items.cn: 古法语 desdignier 意为因不值得而轻视。

items.en: The noun desdain carried the sense of scorn.
items.cn: 名词 desdain 带有鄙弃的意思。

items.en: Middle English disdeyn entered the language as disdain.
items.cn: 中古英语 disdeyn 进入英语成为 disdain。

items.en: The positive form survives as deign, to condescend.
items.cn: 肯定形式保留为 deign，意为屈尊。

note.en: Disdain is the negative of deign; its neighbours share the worthy root or name open contempt.
note.cn: disdain 是 deign 的否定形式；它的邻居要么同「值得」词根，要么指公开的轻视。

dict_mnemonic.text: disdain ＝ dis-（否定）＋ deign（屈尊，拉丁语 dignari「认为值得」，词根 dignus「值得的」）＝连屈尊都不肯，「蔑视、不屑」；同根还有 dignity（尊严）、dignify（使显贵）。

root: 拉丁语 dignus（值得的）→ dignari（认为值得）→ 古法语 desdignier → desdain → 中古英语 disdeyn → disdain

sensesIntro.en: Looking down: a raised chin, a hand pushing a gift away and a mouth that will not answer.
sensesIntro.cn: 往下看：抬起的下巴、推开礼物的手与不肯开口的嘴。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chin lifted high while a hand turns over to push away what is being offered
core.cn: 核心意象：下巴高高抬起，一只手翻过来推开递到面前的东西

branches.en: A raised chin looking down at a cheap gift.
branches.cn: 抬起的下巴斜看廉价礼物。

branches.en: A hand waving an idea away.
branches.cn: 一挥手把想法推开的手。

branches.en: A mouth that refuses to answer.
branches.cn: 拒绝开口的嘴。

branches.en: Both put the other thing below you.
branches.cn: 两者都把对方放到自己之下。

branches.en: Both are refusals others can see.
branches.cn: 两者都是别人看得见的拒绝。

intro.en: Disdain is dis- plus the worthy root; the same root builds deign, dignity and dignify.
intro.cn: disdain 由 dis- 加「值得」这个词根构成；同一个词根也造出 deign、dignity 与 dignify。

latinIntro.en: Latin dignus means worthy, dignari to deem worthy and contemnere to despise.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dignus 意为值得的，dignari 意为认为值得，contemnere 意为轻视。

definition_zh: 疾病；弊病
definition_en: an illness of the body or mind, or a serious problem in a society
core_image: 一片叶子上出现一块褐色斑点，几天后整枝都软了
scene: 叶面上先出现一个褐色小点，几天后整片叶子都软了。The disease spread through the whole orchard in a month.
sceneCN: 这里 disease 指「疾病」（第 1 个义项：身体或精神的病症）；句意是那种病一个月内传遍了整片果园。

senses.title: An illness of the body
senses.definition: an illness that affects the body or mind
senses.definitionCN: 影响身体或精神的病症
senses.example: The disease spread through the orchard.
senses.exampleCN: 那种病传遍了果园。
senses.why: A small spot on one leaf is a whole orchard a month later.
senses.whyCN: 一片叶子上的小点，一个月后就是整片果园。

senses.title: A sickness in society
senses.definition: a serious problem that harms a group or a system
senses.definitionCN: 危害群体或制度的严重问题
senses.example: Greed is a disease of the market.
senses.exampleCN: 贪婪是市场的一种弊病。
senses.why: The same word moves from one body to a body of people.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词从一具身体挪到一群人身上。

intro.en: Disease comes from Old French desaise, a lack of ease, built from des- and aise, comfort.
intro.cn: disease 来自古法语 desaise（不适、不安），由 des-（不）与 aise（安适）构成。

items.en: Adiacens meant lying near, and gave the French word for comfort.
items.cn: adiacens 意为躺卧在旁，后来给出法语里表示安适的词。

items.en: Desaise meant lack of ease or discomfort.
items.cn: 古法语 desaise 指不安适、不舒服。

items.en: English disease first meant unease of any kind.
items.cn: 英语 disease 最初泛指任何不适。

items.en: It narrowed to a named illness of the body.
items.cn: 后来收窄为身体上具体的病症。

items.en: The old sense survives in the idea of a social disease.
items.cn: 旧义在社会弊病这一说法里还留有余影。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on ease, and the meaning group names other words for being unwell.
note.cn: 形近组围绕 ease 构成，近义组列出别的表示身体不适的词。

entries.definition: comfort or freedom from effort
entries.definitionCN: 安适或省力

entries.definition: not calm or comfortable
entries.definitionCN: 不安的

entries.definition: suffering from an illness
entries.definitionCN: 患病的

entries.definition: the state of being unwell
entries.definitionCN: 身体不适的状态

entries.definition: a feeling of being ill
entries.definitionCN: 生病的感觉

entries.definition: a small or lasting disorder
entries.definitionCN: 轻微或长期的病痛

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with one brown spot and end with a word for a broken system.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一个褐色斑点开始，落到一个形容坏制度的词。

normal.en: Dis- plus ease: no ease is disease.
normal.cn: dis 加 ease，失去安适就是病。

normal.en: A garden left alone shows disease first on the oldest leaf.
normal.cn: 无人打理的花园，最老的叶子先显出病。

normal.en: Doctors name a disease so that they can fight one thing.
normal.cn: 医生给病取名，才好集中对付一样东西。

normal.en: A disease of the market hides in plain prices.
normal.cn: 市场的弊病藏在平常的价钱里。

normal.en: Clean water is the cheapest guard against disease.
normal.cn: 干净的水是对抗疾病最便宜的守卫。

abstract.en: Picture one brown spot spreading across a leaf.
abstract.cn: 想象一个褐色斑点爬满一片叶子。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp held over a sick branch at night.
abstract.cn: 想象夜里一盏灯照着病枝。

abstract.en: Picture a word moving from a body to a whole town.
abstract.cn: 想象一个词从一具身体挪到整座城。

examples.en: The disease spread through the whole orchard in a month.
examples.cn: 那种病一个月内传遍了整片果园。

examples.en: Clean water prevents many diseases.
examples.cn: 干净的水能预防许多疾病。

examples.en: Greed is a disease of the market.
examples.cn: 贪婪是市场的一种弊病。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 disease 记成「不自在」：dis 是不，ease 是安适，身体不安适就是病；一个群体不安适，就是弊病。

root: 来自古法语 desaise（不适），由否定前缀 des- 与 aise（安适）构成，而 aise 可追到拉丁语 adiacens（躺卧在旁）。英语最初泛指各种不适，十六世纪起收窄为具体的病症，后来又引申指社会的弊病。

sensesIntro.en: From a body that has lost its ease to a system that has lost its health.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一具失去安适的身体，到一个失去健康的制度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one brown spot on a leaf, and the whole orchard going soft.
core.cn: 核心意象：叶上一个褐色斑点，整片果园慢慢软下去。

branches.en: The first sense is the illness in a living body.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是活身体里的病症。

branches.en: The second sense carries the illness into a system.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把病带进一个制度。

branches.en: Both senses describe something that spreads by itself.
branches.cn: 两个义项都形容会自己蔓延的东西。

branches.en: Both need a name before they can be fought.
branches.cn: 两个义项都要先有名字才好对付。

branches.en: Only the second sense is used about money or power.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项会用在金钱或权力上。

intro.en: Disease belongs to the ease family, where comfort, difficulty and illness share one stem.
intro.cn: disease 属于 ease 一族，安适、容易与疾病共用同一词干。

latinIntro.en: Old French aise, comfort, joins des- to make desaise, and English keeps several relatives of the same stem.
latinIntro.cn: 古法语 aise（安适）加 des- 成为 desaise，英语保留了同一词干的几个亲属。

items.example: He felt uneasy at the door.
A small unease stayed with her.
The diseased tree was cut down.

definition_zh: v. 使失去权力；剥夺…的影响力；使无权
definition_en: to take power, authority or confidence away from a person or group
core_image: 一个人手里的印章被收走，桌上的名牌被换成空白的；扩音器的插头被拔掉
scene: 新规章让基层员工失去了决定权。The new rules disempower front-line staff.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：新规章把决定权从基层员工手里收走。

pos.zh: 使失去权力；剥夺…的影响力；使无权

senses.title: Take away authority
senses.definition: to remove the power or authority that a person or group had
senses.definitionCN: （动词）拿走个人或群体原本拥有的权力
senses.example: The new rules disempower front-line staff.
senses.exampleCN: 新规章让基层员工失去了决定权。
senses.why: A stamp lifted out of an open hand.
senses.whyCN: 一枚印章从摊开的手里被拿走。

senses.title: Remove influence
senses.definition: to make a person or group unable to affect decisions
senses.definitionCN: （动词）使个人或群体无法影响决定
senses.example: The merger disempowered the local committee.
senses.exampleCN: 合并让地方委员会失去了影响力。
senses.why: A microphone plug pulled out of the wall.
senses.whyCN: 一个麦克风插头从墙上被拔掉。

senses.title: Drain confidence
senses.definition: to make someone feel unable to act or speak up
senses.definitionCN: （动词）让某人觉得自己无法行动或发声
senses.example: Years of silence left the workers disempowered.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的沉默让工人们觉得自己毫无分量。
senses.why: A desk nameplate swapped for a blank one.
senses.whyCN: 桌上的名牌被换成一块空白的。

intro.en: Disempower is dis- plus empower; empower is em- plus power, which goes back through Old French poer to Latin posse, to be able.
intro.cn: disempower 由 dis-（去掉）加 empower（赋权）构成；empower 是 em-（使）加 power（力量），power 经古法语 poer 上溯拉丁语 posse「能够」。

items.en: Latin posse means to be able or have power.
items.cn: 拉丁语 posse 意为能够、有权力。

items.en: Old French poer carried the sense of ability.
items.cn: 古法语 poer 带有能力的意思。

items.en: Middle English power entered from Old French.
items.cn: 中古英语 power 从古法语进入英语。

items.en: The prefix em- gave empower, to give power to.
items.cn: 前缀 em- 造出 empower，意为赋予权力。

items.en: Dis- was added in modern use to give disempower.
items.cn: 现代用法中加上 dis- 得到 disempower。

items.en: The word became common in writing on rights and work.
items.cn: 这个词在关于权利与工作的论述中变得常见。

note.en: Disempower is empower reversed; its neighbours either share the power root or mean pushing people aside.
note.cn: disempower 是 empower 的反向；它的邻居要么同「权力」词根，要么表示把人推到一边。

entries.definition: to give someone power or confidence to act
entries.definitionCN: 给某人行动或发声的权力与底气

entries.definition: the process of giving power or confidence
entries.definitionCN: 赋予权力或底气的过程

entries.definition: the process of taking power away
entries.definitionCN: 剥夺权力的过程

entries.definition: to deprive someone of a right, especially the vote
entries.definitionCN: 剥夺某人的权利，尤指选举权

entries.definition: to treat a group as unimportant and without influence
entries.definitionCN: 把某个群体当成不重要、没有影响力的

entries.definition: to make someone or something less strong
entries.definitionCN: 使某人或某物变弱

normalIntro.cn: 五个权力被拔掉插头的画面。

normal.en: A microphone plug pulled out of the wall.
normal.cn: 一个麦克风插头从墙上被拔掉。

normal.en: A desk nameplate swapped for a blank one.
normal.cn: 桌上的名牌被换成一块空白的。

normal.en: A voting card cut in half at the desk.
normal.cn: 一张选民卡在柜台被剪成两半。

normal.en: A chair removed from the decision table.
normal.cn: 一把椅子从决策桌边被搬走。

abstract.en: A stamp lifted out of an open hand.
abstract.cn: 一枚印章从摊开的手里被拿走。

abstract.en: A microphone plug pulled out of the wall.
abstract.cn: 一个麦克风插头从墙上被拔掉。

abstract.en: A desk nameplate swapped for a blank one.
abstract.cn: 桌上的名牌被换成一块空白的。

examples.en: The reform disempowered local councils.
examples.cn: 改革让地方议会失去了权力。

examples.en: She felt disempowered in the meeting.
examples.cn: 她在那场会议里觉得自己毫无分量。

examples.en: Such rules disempower the people they claim to help.
examples.cn: 这样的规章反而剥夺了它们声称要帮助的人的权力。

dict_mnemonic.text: disempower ＝ dis-（去掉）＋ empower（赋权）＝把权力拿掉；empower ＝ em-（使）＋ power（力量，古法语 poer，拉丁语 posse「能够」），所以 disempower 就是「使人不再能够」。

root: 拉丁语 posse（能够）→ 古法语 poer → 中古英语 power → em- ＋ power ＝ empower → 加 dis- 成 disempower

sensesIntro.en: Power unplugged: a stamp taken from a hand, a microphone cut off and a nameplate left blank.
sensesIntro.cn: 被拔掉的权力：从手里收走的印章、被切断的麦克风与留白的名牌。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stamp lifted out of an open hand while a microphone plug is pulled from the wall
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚印章从摊开的手里被拿走，同时麦克风插头从墙上被拔掉

branches.en: Rules taking the stamp from front-line staff.
branches.cn: 规章把印章从基层员工手里收走。

branches.en: A committee whose microphone is unplugged.
branches.cn: 麦克风被拔掉插头的委员会。

branches.en: Workers left with a blank nameplate.
branches.cn: 只剩一块空白名牌的工人。

branches.en: Both remove the ability to decide.
branches.cn: 两者都拿走了做决定的能力。

branches.en: Both leave people unable to be heard.
branches.cn: 两者都让人无法被听见。

intro.en: Disempower is dis- plus empower; the able root also builds power, powerful and powerless.
intro.cn: disempower 由 dis- 加 empower 构成；能够这个词根也造出 power、powerful 与 powerless。

latinIntro.en: Latin posse means to be able, potis powerful, and Old French franc free.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 posse 意为能够，potis 意为有权力的，古法语 franc 意为自由的。

definition_zh: n. 失望；不抱幻想；醒悟；幻灭
definition_en: the feeling of being disappointed because something is not as good as you believed
core_image: 舞台上的灯突然全亮，布景后面的木架和电线露出来；魔法棒掉在地上变成普通木棍
scene: 选民对政治日益幻灭。There is growing disenchantment with politics.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：选民原先的期待落空，不再相信那套说法。

forms.label: 复数（多起失望之事，较少用）

senses.title: Loss of illusion
senses.definition: the feeling that something you admired is not as good as you thought
senses.definitionCN: （名词）发现自己欣赏的东西并不如原先所想的那种感觉
senses.example: There is growing disenchantment with politics.
senses.exampleCN: 选民对政治日益幻灭。
senses.why: Stage lights coming up to show the wooden frame behind the set.
senses.whyCN: 舞台灯全亮，露出布景后面的木架。

senses.title: Disappointment with a person
senses.definition: a loss of enthusiasm for someone you once supported
senses.definitionCN: （名词）对曾经支持的人失去热情
senses.example: Her disenchantment with the leader was complete.
senses.exampleCN: 她对那位领袖彻底失望了。
senses.why: A campaign badge dropped into a drawer.
senses.whyCN: 一枚竞选徽章被丢进抽屉。

senses.title: A sober view
senses.definition: the state of seeing things as they are, without romantic belief
senses.definitionCN: （名词）不再带着浪漫想象、如实看待事物的状态
senses.example: He spoke with the disenchantment of an old insider.
senses.exampleCN: 他说话时带着老内部人那种不再抱幻想的清醒。
senses.why: A magic wand lying on the floor as a plain stick.
senses.whyCN: 一根魔法棒掉在地上，成了普通木棍。

intro.en: Disenchantment is dis- plus enchantment; enchant comes from Old French enchanter, from Latin incantare, to sing a spell over, from in- plus cantare, to sing.
intro.cn: disenchantment 由 dis-（去掉）加 enchantment（着迷、魔法）构成；enchant 来自古法语 enchanter，上溯拉丁语 incantare「对着唱咒语」，由 in- 加 cantare「唱」组成。

items.en: Latin cantare means to sing.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cantare 意为唱。

items.en: Incantare meant to sing a spell over someone.
items.cn: incantare 意为对某人唱咒语。

items.en: Old French enchanter carried the sense of charming by song.
items.cn: 古法语 enchanter 带有用歌声迷惑的意思。

items.en: Enchant entered English for delighting as if by magic.
items.cn: enchant 进入英语，表示像施了魔法一样使人着迷。

items.en: Dis- gave disenchant, to remove the spell.
items.cn: dis- 造出 disenchant，意为把魔法去掉。

items.en: The suffix -ment produced disenchantment, the state of being disenchanted.
items.cn: 后缀 -ment 造出 disenchantment，指不再着迷的状态。

note.en: Disenchantment is enchantment with the spell removed; its neighbours share the sing root or name lost belief.
note.cn: disenchantment 是把魔法去掉的 enchantment；它的邻居要么同「唱」词根，要么指失去的信念。

entries.definition: a feeling of great delight, as if under a spell
entries.definitionCN: 像中了魔法一般的极大愉悦

entries.definition: no longer believing in the value of something
entries.definitionCN: 不再相信某事物价值的

entries.definition: to free someone from an illusion or spell
entries.definitionCN: 使某人从幻想或魔法中清醒过来

entries.definition: the feeling that something is not as good as believed
entries.definitionCN: 发现某事不如原先所想的感觉

entries.definition: sadness because hopes were not met
entries.definitionCN: 因为期待落空而产生的难过

entries.definition: a belief that people act only from self interest
entries.definitionCN: 认为人只出于私利行事的态度

normalIntro.cn: 五个魔法失效的画面。

normal.en: A magic wand lying on the floor as a plain stick.
